messages:
sara_infra: Heads-up — we saw a burst of NVIDIA Xid 13 and 31 on rack10-12 right after the maintenance window at ~03:15 UTC. Affected hosts are serving embeddings-heavy tenant 'vectorly', spikes line up with their larger batch sizes. Can we triage? :eyes:

jon_sre: How many GPUs and which codes? Any ECC alerts?

sara_infra: Short snippets from dmesg and nvidia-smi during the window:
```
[03:22:11] NVRM: Xid (13) GPU 0: 13, PID 22841, GPU 0x00000000
[03:22:12] NVRM: Xid (31) GPU 1: 31, PID 22902, SGID 0x1
[03:22:12] nv_hostnet: link reset on peer 0x7fcb

# nvidia-smi pmon -c 1
# gpu   pid  type    sm   mem   enc   dec
    0 22841 C      99%  60%
    1 22902 C      92%  58%
```
No ECC OOPS in syslog but some NVLink peer resets.

mayank: Interesting — NVLink resets + Xid 31 tends to point at peer comms or thermal/power glitches. Did we change BIOS/firmware or driver during the window?

kelsey: deploy-bot rolled the GPU driver update (v525->v530) to rack10-12 at 03:15 as a staggered push. I flagged it in the deploy channel.

deploy-bot: driver-rollout-batch: applied driver v530 to hosts rack10-{10..12} at 2026-03-17T03:15:14Z by infra-ops. (change-id: drv-roll-2026-03-17-03)

jon_sre: That matches timing. Two paths: isolate host-level regressions (drain + repro) or roll back driver if easy. Can we reproduce by replaying vectorly workload with high batch?

sara_infra: Repro steps we used locally (shortened):
1) pin to rack10 GPUs
2) run embedding job with batch_size=1024, prefetched KV cache enabled
3) watch for NVHost resets in dmesg

We got Xid 13 around 30-90s after sustained high token-rate.

mayank: Hypothesis: driver v530 changes NVLink timeout/peer handling + our autoscaler bumped batch/concurrency. Quick mitigations: reduce batch_size to 256 for vectorly, disable peer-to-peer for that job, and roll affected hosts to previous driver.

kelsey: I can start a rolling drain for rack10-12, collect /var/crash and GPU core dumps, then rerun vectorly with batch=256. Will do a 5-host-at-a-time drain to limit impact.

jon_sre: Commands that helped in past incidents:
```bash
# mark node unsched and drain pods/containers
sudo /usr/local/bin/drain-node.sh rack10-11
# clear GPU state (careful in prod)
sudo nvidia-smi --gpu-reset -i 0
# enable persistence mode for stability
sudo nvidia-smi -pm ENABLED
```
Also capture `dmesg | grep -i nv` and `journalctl -k --since "5 minutes ago"`

sara_infra: I'll coordinate with vectorly SRE to throttle their job while we triage. Also collecting `nvidia-bug-report.sh` outputs from the drained hosts.

deploy-bot: opsnote: rollback option available (driver v525) via change set drv-roll-2026-03-17-03-rev. Contact infra-lead to trigger.

mayank: If rollback is needed, prefer rolling back whole rack, not single host — NVLink peer incompatibilities can persist if peers mismatch.

kelsey: Started drain on rack10-10 -> rack10-11 -> rack10-12. Will attach crash bundles here once uploaded. ETA 45m.

ops-bot: Created incident INC-2026-1287 for GPU-fleet Xid spikes and linked on-call.

sara_infra: Quick update after first two hosts drained: Xid spikes stopped on remaining hosts, vectorly reduced batch to 256 and errors did not reappear in 20m. Looks like combination of driver + high batch.

jon_sre: Good sign. Next steps: 1) finish drain and collect bug reports 2) run driver rollback on rack10 if we see any recurrence 3) add workload-level guardrails (max_batch override) for tenants that cause saturation.

mayank: I'll open a proposal to add a runtime flag to disable GPU peer-to-peer per-job in the scheduler and auto-throttle batch when GPU errors spike.

kelsey: Uploaded crash bundles to s3://redwood-gpu-crash/rack10/2026-03-17/. Links: https://s3.internal/.../bundle-rack10-10.tar.gz

sara_infra: Final note — no ECC counts changed, so this looks non-ECC (comms/driver) rather than memory errors. Marking as driver-induced until proven otherwise.

jon_sre: Thanks all. Leave this thread open; we'll update INC-2026-1287 with postmortem after root cause confirmed. :white_check_mark:
